text: ===== README.md ===== 1 # Ocean Surface 2 3 The client face of [Ocean OS](https://github.com/Risingtides-dev/ocean-os). 4 One Rust + Leptos app, built once via Trunk and shipped to two hosts: the 5 browser PWA and the Tauri native shell — both load the same `dist/` WASM bundle. 6 A Chrome extension wraps that same bundle. Native macOS is delivered by the 7 Tauri 2.x shell (`crates/ocean-tauri`), not a separate GPUI app; the legacy 8 GPUI desktop app (`crates/ocean-gui`) is soft-deprecated (source retained for 9 mining into the Tauri Rust backend). 10 11 Cross-repo routing and ownership map: [`docs/OCEAN_PROJECT_MAP.md`](docs/OCEAN_PROJECT_MAP.md). 12 13 | Target | How | Why | 14 |---|---|---| 15 | Native desktop (Tauri) | `./run-tauri.sh` (or `cd crates/ocean-tauri && cargo tauri dev`) | Tauri 2.x shell loading the same `dist/` Leptos bundle as the browser | 16 | Browser PWA | `trunk serve` or `./run-surface.sh` | desktop/mobile browser access over the daemon API | 17 | Chrome extension | `extension/` wrapper | browser-side panel with explicit `surface-extension` context | 18 | Web proxy | `cargo run -p ocean-surface-proxy` | serves web bundle, config, STT/TTS, and daemon reverse proxy | 19 20 All targets are thin clients over `ocean-daemon`. None hold agent logic or 21 session authority, and none hold provider credentials. Voice STT/TTS 22 credentials are owned by ocean-os (daemon endpoints `/v1/voice/stt` and 23 `/v1/voice/tts`); the proxy forwards to the daemon transparently. They speak 24 the daemon's product agent API: 25 26 ``` 27 POST /v1/agent/sessions 28 GET /v1/agent/events?session_id= 29 POST /v1/agent/turns { prompt, cwd, session_id, project_id?, client_type, ... } 30 ``` 31 32 Surfaces create or choose a session before posting turns. They do not adopt a 33 session from global SSE. Cross-surface sharing is explicit: attach both 34 surfaces to the same `session_id`. 35 36 ## Daemon API 37 38 All surfaces drive the daemon over the same HTTP+SSE product agent API. The 39 wire shapes the surfaces send live in 40 [`crates/ocean-surface-ui/src/daemon.rs`](crates/ocean-surface-ui/src/daemon.rs); 41 the daemon side is `ocean-os`. The daemon listens on `127.0.0.1:4780` by 42 default (`OCEAN_BIND` to override); surfaces resolve it via `OCEAN_DAEMON_URL`. 43 44 ### `POST /v1/agent/sessions` 45 46 Create (or reuse) a session before the first turn. Body 47 (`AgentSessionCreateRequest`): 48 49 | Field | Type | Notes | 50 | ---------------- | ---------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | 51 | `workspace_root` | `string` | **Required** workspace anchor. (No serde alias for `cwd` — sending `cwd` fails to deserialize.) | 52 | `project_id` | `string?` | Optional project binding. | 53 | `client_type` | `string?` | The originating surface (`surface-web`, `surface-extension`, …). | 54 55 Returns the `session_id`. Surfaces then subscribe with 56 `GET /v1/agent/events?session_id=` and send that `session_id` on every 57 turn. 58 59 ### `POST /v1/agent/turns` 60 61 Start a turn. The POST returns once the turn completes but carries only 62 metadata — reply text, tool calls, and ids arrive over the SSE stream. Body 63 (`AgentTurnRequest`): 64 65 | Field | Type | Notes | 66 | ---------------- | ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | 67 | `prompt` | `string` | The user/turn prompt. | 68 | `cwd` | `string` | Working directory for the turn. The web client sends `"/"` and relies on `project_id` for the real workspace. | 69 | `session_id` | `string?` | The session this turn belongs to. Omitted only when the daemon should mint one. | 70 | `project_id` | `string?` | Selected project. When set, the daemon binds the turn to the project's `workspace_root`. | 71 | `client_type` | `string?` | The originating surface, so the agent can adapt per surface (`surface-web`, `surface-extension`, …). | 72 | `guidance` | `string[]?` | Optional guidance hints passed to the agent (e.g. active-tab context, `"focus on tests"`). Added in OCEAN-61. | 73 | `room_id` | `string?` | Optional room identifier for Track-0 room-scoped turns. Added in OCEAN-61. Not yet exposed in the web UI. | 74 | `thinking_level` | `string?` | Per-turn reasoning-effort override, serialized as the daemon's lowercase `ThinkingLevel` string. `None` leaves the daemon's global default in force. Added in OCEAN-61. Not yet exposed in the web UI. | 75 | `model_id` | `string?` | Per-session / per-turn model override (OCEAN-36). Mirrors the daemon's `model_id: Option`. `None` leaves the session/daemon default model in force. Added to the surface wire shape in OCEAN-61. Not yet exposed in the web UI. | 76 77 All `Option` fields are `skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none"`, so they are 78 omitted from the JSON body when unset rather than sent as `null`. 79 80 ### `GET /v1/agent/events?session_id=` 81 82 Session-scoped SSE stream of `AgentTurnEvent`s (assistant text, tool calls, 83 permission requests, completion). Surfaces must subscribe scoped to their own 84 `session_id` and must not adopt active sessions from the global SSE stream. 85 86 ## Workspace 87 88 | Path | Role | 89 | ------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- | 90 | `crates/ocean-surface-ui/` | canonical Leptos UI (CSR/WASM) for web/PWA/extension/Tauri. | 91 | `crates/ocean-tauri/` | Tauri 2.x native desktop shell; loads the same `dist/` bundle as the browser PWA. | 92 | `crates/ocean-surface-proxy/` | axum service: forwards voice STT/TTS to the daemon, serves the WASM bundle. | 93 | `extension/` | Chrome extension wrapper around the Leptos surface. | 94 | `legacy-voice/` | Reference: the JS voice client (PR #22). Deleted once ported. | 95 | `crates/ocean-gui/` | legacy GPUI native desktop app and tldraw canvas host (soft-deprecated, source retained for mining). | 96 | `crates/ocean-gui/canvas-web/` | tldraw/web bundle loaded by the GPUI canvas host (legacy). | 97 98 ## Dev loop 99 100 ### One command (recommended) 101 102 The daemon must be running (in `../ocean-os`: `cargo run -p ocean-daemon --release`). Then: 103 104 ```sh 105 # Build the wasm bundle + serve it and the proxy from one binary: 106 ./run-surface.sh 107 # → open http://:8790 (works on a phone via the tailnet IP) 108 109 # Or build dist/ + launch the Tauri native desktop shell (loads the same bundle): 110 ./run-tauri.sh 111 ``` 112 113 `run-surface.sh` binds `0.0.0.0:8790` by default. Override with 114 `OCEAN_SURFACE_BIND`, `OCEAN_DAEMON_URL`, `OCEAN_VOICE_PROFILE`. 115 116 ### Verify before you open the browser 117 118 ```sh 119 ./smoke.sh # health, /api/config, chat round-trip, + live STT/TTS (daemon must be running) 120 ``` 121 122 5/5 green means every wired path works; then the browser check is just UI/mic confirmation. 123 124 ### Native desktop (Tauri) 125 126 ```sh 127 ./run-tauri.sh # build dist/ + launch the Tauri shell 128 cd crates/ocean-tauri && cargo tauri dev # or, run dev mode directly 129 ``` 130 131 Tauri loads the same `dist/` Leptos bundle the browser ships; its Rust backend 132 adds native folder dialogs and path watcher (replacing the GPUI crate's `rfd`/ 133 `notify`). The canvas+LiveKit design intent is documented in 134 [`docs/OCEAN_GPUI_CANVAS_LIVEKIT_SPEC.md`](docs/OCEAN_GPUI_CANVAS_LIVEKIT_SPEC.md) 135 (now a historical reference; the implementation surface is Leptos+Tauri). 136 137 ### Live-reload web dev 138 139 ```sh 140 trunk serve --open # → http://localhost:8080 141 OCEAN_DAEMON_URL=http://mac-mini.tailnet:4780 trunk serve --open # remote daemon 142 ``` 143 144 Note: `trunk serve` serves the UI but NOT the proxy, so voice (`/api/stt`, 145 `/api/tts`) and `/api/config` need `run-surface.sh`. Text chat works under 146 both. 147 148 ## Voice — daemon-owned 149 150 Voice STT/TTS provider credentials are owned by `ocean-os` (daemon endpoints 151 `/v1/voice/stt` and `/v1/voice/tts`). The proxy forwards `/api/stt` and 152 `/api/tts` to the daemon transparently; the browser never sees a credential. 153 Set `XAI_API_KEY` in the daemon's environment (or configure the credential 154 via ocean-os's provider auth file). The proxy no longer reads or stores an 155 xAI key. 156 157 `GET /api/config` reports `has_auth`; the UI fetches it on boot so no URL or credential is ever typed in the browser. 158 159 ## Roadmap 160 161 - Done: web/PWA chat, SSE transcript, model picker, session picker, proxy, 162 voice STT/TTS, Chrome extension bootstrap, provider-backed STT/TTS moved 163 to daemon-owned voice endpoints in `ocean-os` (proxy no longer holds xAI key). 164 - In progress: Tauri native shell (loads the same `dist/` bundle), explicit 165 session scoping, Leptos canvas, canvas ledger, LiveKit presence controls. 166 - Next: reliable canvas IPC for Leptos+Tauri, tldraw render commands, LiveKit 167 mic/camera participation, surface-state injection into agent turns, native 168 LiveKit Rust client behind a Tauri feature flag. 169 170 ## Provenance 171 172 The voice work in `legacy-voice/` was originally proposed as PR #22 in `ocean-os`.      3	/**
     4	 * One deterministic difficulty curve for the whole mission. Progress is the
     5	 * distance travelled over the 420m route, clamped to [0, 1]. Every multiplier

     7	 */
     8	export const LEVEL_LENGTH = 420
     9	
    10	export interface Difficulty {
    11	  progress: number
    12	  healthMultiplier: number
    13	  fireIntervalMultiplier: number
    14	  projectileSpeed: number
    15	  aimLead: number
    16	  accuracy: number
    17	  waveDensity: number
    18	  formationScale: number

    20	
    21	export function normalizedLevelProgress(distance: number) {
    22	  return THREE.MathUtils.clamp(distance / LEVEL_LENGTH, 0, 1)
    23	}
    24	
    25	export function getDifficulty(progress: number): Difficulty {
    26	  const p = THREE.MathUtils.clamp(progress, 0, 1)
    27	  return {
    28	    progress: p,
    29	    healthMultiplier: 1 + p * 0.9,
    30	    fireIntervalMultiplier: 1 - p * 0.45,
    31	    projectileSpeed: 42 + p * 21,
    32	    aimLead: 0.15 + p * 0.85,
    33	    accuracy: 0.34 + p * 0.6,
    34	    waveDensity: 1 + p * 0.5,
    35	    formationScale: 1 + p * 0.22,
    36	  }
    37	}

    40	  return Math.max(1, Math.ceil(baseHealth * difficulty.healthMultiplier))
    41	}

    51	    health: scaledHealth(enemy.health, difficulty),
    52	  }))
    53	  const extraCount = Math.max(0, Math.ceil((difficulty.waveDensity - 1) * enemies.length))

## Review
- Correct:
  - `src/game/difficulty.ts:21-36` correctly clamps normalized progress to `[0,1]`; endpoint multipliers are health `1.9x`, cadence `0.55x`, projectile speed `63`, lead `1.0`, accuracy `94%`, density `1.5x`, formation `1.22x`.
  - Targeting is deterministic: `src/game/Enemy.tsx:51-60` uses player position/velocity, bounded prediction, and seeded error; no runtime randomness.
  - Boss expiry and teammate rescue paths are wired in `src/game/Game.tsx:217-229`; kills restore threatened teammates and expiry marks them down.
  - `npm run build` passed (`tsc --noEmit` and Vite build).

- Blocker:
  - `src/game/difficulty.ts:53-64`: `ceil((waveDensity - 1) * enemies.length)` exceeds the declared density cap. A 3-enemy wave at maximum density becomes 5 enemies (`1.67x`, not `1.5x`). At any positive progress, a 3-enemy wave already gets one extra enemy because `ceil(positive fraction) = 1`.
  - `src/game/difficulty.ts:48-62`: formation scaling is not bounded to the playable envelope. Late waves can spawn at approximately `x = ±9.04`, while `src/game/Arwing.tsx:6-8` limits the player to `±7.2`. These enemies may be impossible to hit under `src/game/Game.tsx:469-475`’s `1.1` collision radius.
  - `src/game/Enemy.tsx:53-58`: the prediction is clamped relative to the current player position, not to the absolute playable envelope, and seeded error is added after clamping. Predictions can therefore leave the envelope.

- Note:
  - `src/game/difficulty.ts:39-40`: `ceil` causes immediate health jumps. A base-1 scout becomes 2 HP at any progress above zero; this is much sharper than the documented smooth `1.9x` curve.
  - `src/game/Enemy.tsx:51-52` is not a true intercept solve. It uses `range / projectileSpeed`, then leads by `velocity * t * aimLead`. A true solve should use the quadratic relative-motion equation `|r + vt| = speed*t`; current math under/over-leads at high player velocity.
  - `src/game/Enemy.tsx:56-58`: all enemies with equal-length IDs share the same deterministic error sequence, causing synchronized miss/hit patterns.
  - `src/game/Enemy.tsx:46-47`: turret cadence is calculated but turrets are explicitly prevented from firing; verify this is intentional.
  - No algorithm tests are present. Add pure tests for endpoint curves, density counts, envelope bounds, deterministic wave output, intercept edge cases, teammate rescue, and boss expiry.
  - Collision is discrete rather than swept (`src/game/Game.tsx:466-495`), so high-speed projectiles can tunnel through targets at low frame rates.

## Review
- Correct:
  - `src/game/difficulty.ts:21-36` correctly clamps normalized progress to `[0,1]`; endpoint multipliers are health `1.9x`, cadence `0.55x`, projectile speed `63`, lead `1.0`, accuracy `94%`, density `1.5x`, formation `1.22x`.
  - Targeting is deterministic: `src/game/Enemy.tsx:51-60` uses player position/velocity, bounded prediction, and seeded error; no runtime randomness.
  - Boss expiry and teammate rescue paths are wired in `src/game/Game.tsx:217-229`; kills restore threatened teammates and expiry marks them down.
  - `npm run build` passed (`tsc --noEmit` and Vite build).

- Blocker:
  - `src/game/difficulty.ts:53-64`: `ceil((waveDensity - 1) * enemies.length)` exceeds the declared density cap. A 3-enemy wave at maximum density becomes 5 enemies (`1.67x`, not `1.5x`). At any positive progress, a 3-enemy wave already gets one extra enemy because `ceil(positive fraction) = 1`.
  - `src/game/difficulty.ts:48-62`: formation scaling is not bounded to the playable envelope. Late waves can spawn at approximately `x = ±9.04`, while `src/game/Arwing.tsx:6-8` limits the player to `±7.2`. These enemies may be impossible to hit under `src/game/Game.tsx:469-475`’s `1.1` collision radius.
  - `src/game/Enemy.tsx:53-58`: the prediction is clamped relative to the current player position, not to the absolute playable envelope, and seeded error is added after clamping. Predictions can therefore leave the envelope.

- Note:
  - `src/game/difficulty.ts:39-40`: `ceil` causes immediate health jumps. A base-1 scout becomes 2 HP at any progress above zero; this is much sharper than the documented smooth `1.9x` curve.
  - `src/game/Enemy.tsx:51-52` is not a true intercept solve. It uses `range / projectileSpeed`, then leads by `velocity * t * aimLead`. A true solve should use the quadratic relative-motion equation `|r + vt| = speed*t`; current math under/over-leads at high player velocity.
  - `src/game/Enemy.tsx:56-58`: all enemies with equal-length IDs share the same deterministic error sequence, causing synchronized miss/hit patterns.
  - `src/game/Enemy.tsx:46-47`: turret cadence is calculated but turrets are explicitly prevented from firing; verify this is intentional.
  - No algorithm tests are present. Add pure tests for endpoint curves, density counts, envelope bounds, deterministic wave output, intercept edge cases, teammate rescue, and boss expiry.
  - Collision is discrete rather than swept (`src/game/Game.tsx:466-495`), so high-speed projectiles can tunnel through targets at low frame rates.
